harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 as tmpfs mounts with noexec,nosuid,nodev via /etc/fstab, applied live without a reboot, functionally verified the execution restriction, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a pre-restart boot_id baseline, rebooted node1 natively, polled until reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (fresh boot, uptime 0 min), and re-verified both mounts still enforce noexec,nosuid,nodev post-reboot with a functional exec-blocked test.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline mount state of /tmp and /dev/shm and existing /etc/fstab on node1
Backed up /etc/fstab and appended tmpfs entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec
Ran systemctl daemon-reload, mounted /tmp fresh, and remounted /dev/shm to apply the new options live
Verified via findmnt that both mounts show nosuid,nodev,noexec
Functionally proved noexec by copying /bin/true into /tmp and /dev/shm, chmod +x, and confirming execution returns Permission denied (exit 126)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline from /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1 via a backgrounded delayed command so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 with repeated exec calls until it became reachable again
Confirmed changed boot_id and uptime 0 min, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /tmp and /dev/shm mount options persisted across reboot via fstab (no manual remount needed) and re-ran the exec-block functional test

evidence.requirement: Baseline state before changes: /tmp not separately mounted, /dev/shm lacked noexec
evidence.summary: findmnt/fstab/systemctl showed /tmp was part of the root filesystem (no separate mount) and /dev/shm was tmpfs with only nosuid,nodev (no noexec) before any changes

evidence.requirement: Persist noexec,nosuid,nodev for /tmp and /dev/shm across reboots (fstab configuration)
evidence.summary: Appended tmpfs fstab entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec after backing up the original fstab

evidence.requirement: Apply the hardened mount options live and confirm active options
evidence.summary: systemctl daemon-reload, mount /tmp, and remount /dev/shm applied the new options; findmnt confirmed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on both mounts

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that program execution is ignored/blocked on /tmp and /dev/shm (pre-reboot)
evidence.summary: Copied and chmod +x'd /bin/true into /tmp and /dev/shm; executing it returned 'Permission denied' with exit code 126 on both, proving noexec is enforced

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restart (boot identity + mount health)
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (34027437-307c-4f58-bdb2-1fe626bb2d66) and confirmed /tmp and /dev/shm both showed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec via findmnt immediately before the restart

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection; node actually goes down
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot was scheduled via a backgrounded delayed command, returning 'reboot scheduled' successfully; the immediate next probe failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Poll until node1 is reachable again after restart
evidence.summary: Repeated probes timed out/reset while node1 was rebooting, then succeeded once the node came back online

evidence.requirement: Proof that boot identity changed (real restart, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id was 92b019c3-f0f4-4b9f-b211-4f7631680910, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, with uptime showing 'up 0 min', directly proving a fresh boot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: mount options for /tmp and /dev/shm persisted and are healthy
evidence.summary: findmnt after reboot showed /tmp and /dev/shm both still mounted with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec, confirming the fstab entries survived reboot without manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional proof that noexec/nosuid/nodev are still enforced
evidence.summary: After reboot, copying and executing a test binary from /tmp and /dev/shm again returned 'Permission denied' (exit 126) on both, confirming the hardening persisted through the restart

attempts.summary: Configured /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 as tmpfs mounts with noexec,nosuid,nodev via /etc/fstab, applied live without a reboot, functionally verified the execution restriction, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a pre-restart boot_id baseline, rebooted node1 natively, polled until reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (fresh boot, uptime 0 min), and re-verified both mounts still enforce noexec,nosuid,nodev post-reboot with a functional exec-blocked test.
